## The question

**Is being more attractive associated with earning more, even after accounting for intelligence? This matters for labor economists and HR professionals, since a salary bonus for looks that ability doesn't explain could point to bias in the workplace. Our data comes from the Wisconsin Longitudinal Study, where each observation is a 1957 Wisconsin high school graduate. The response is annual income, and the predictors are perceived attractiveness, height, IQ, sex, BMI, and waist circumference.

One important limitation is that attractiveness was rated from yearbook photos, so it is a subjective measure. The cohort is also a specific group from one place and time, which limits how far the results generalize.**
